findings.rationale: Local calibration is far off while local AUC is normal (0.808): observed prevalence 0.374 vs mean predicted 0.189 at round 20 (CITL -0.18, citl_z -13.4, ECE z +12). Round-by-round CITL is negative from round 1 onward (-0.23 at round 1) with no feature drift (shift_sd about 0 in most rounds), so the shift is in outcome prevalence from the start. The subgroup O/E ratio is about 2 in both sex groups, i.e. a uniform prevalence excess, not one under-recorded subgroup. Update anomalies (median norm ratio 3.75, mean cos -0.28) are consistent with the client training away from a miscalibrated label distribution rather than with poisoning, since its local performance is abnormal.

Observed prevalence 0.304 vs mean predicted 0.143 at round 20 (CITL -0.16, citl_z -11.2, ECE z +8.6, prevalence z +5.0) with normal local AUC (0.831). Observed prevalence is about 0.3 in every round including round 1 (0.316), so the excess is present from the start. Subgroup O/E is about 2 in both sex groups (1.77 to 2.14), a uniform prevalence mismatch rather than subgroup under-recording. Update anomalies (median norm ratio 2.69, mean cos -0.24) follow from the miscalibrated labels, not from a separate manipulation.

Observed prevalence 0.324 vs mean predicted 0.165 at round 20 (CITL -0.158, citl_z -12.4, ECE z +11.5, prevalence z +5.7) with normal local AUC (0.817). CITL is persistently negative from round 4 onward (-0.20 at round 4) and the prevalence stays around 0.29-0.36 across rounds, so the mismatch is present throughout; the exact onset is uncertain because per-round CITL is noisy at the epsilon used. Subgroup O/E is about 2 in both sex groups, a uniform prevalence excess. Its update anomalies (median norm ratio 5.06, mean cos -0.33) are consistent with training on miscalibrated labels.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed with a narrower drift query on the suspects. Three clients (AZ, UT, WA) stand clearly apart: their local CITL is about -0.16 to -0.18 (z of about -11 to -13), observed prevalence is about 0.30-0.37 against predicted 0.14-0.19, local AUC is normal, their feature distributions do not drift, and their O/E ratios are about 2 uniformly across sex, age and income groups. This matches prevalence_shift, not subgroup bias or label noise. Their update anomalies (large norms, negative cosine) are consistent with training on miscalibrated labels, and their local performance is abnormal, so I did not classify them as poisoning. Reported onset is round 1 for all three; WA's exact onset is uncertain. Several other clients (GU, AL, AK, VI, NC, NM, NH, DC, PR, ME, NV) show single or weak outliers at |z_noise| of about 3-4.5 on small-sample statistics (e.g. GU's low update cosine and tail values, AL's Sex mean and Stroke shift). These are within the range expected from noise across about 50 clients and dozens of statistics, and none reached the |z|>=6 or two-tool corroboration bar, so they are not reported. No drift, label_noise, subgroup_bias, missing_artefact, free_rider, explanation_instability or poisoning signal was confirmed. The attribution-churn tool was not used. Budget was fully spent (20.0).
